more_info.uses: EU permissions include meal replacement for weight control as referred to in Commission Regulation (EU) no 432/2012, flavoured drinks, flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products, edible ices. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.origin: Made by catalytic hydrogenation of neohesperidin. This is a chemically modified flavonoid preparation.
more_info.side_effects:
Reported food-use estimates were below the limit.
The assessment used an animal no-effect dose and an additional factor for limited-duration testing.
more_info.overview: Neohesperidine dihydrochalcone is classified in food technology as a flavour enhancer. Its technological role is to strengthen existing flavours.
